ledger_validation: All captured and final valid histories have contiguous 1-based integer seq, correct provider/version/domain-separated recomputed hashes/links, no duplicate authorization IDs, matching snapshots. S02 intentionally invalid ledgers preserved unmodified.

snapshot_reconciliation.actual_implementation: Exact match accepted; only a verified ledger-prefix snapshot may safe-forward. Missing cache rebuilds. Ahead, equal-sequence divergence, non-prefix older state and parseable invalid schema fail closed. Malformed JSON bytes are durably preserved before documented cache recovery; unreadable state fails closed.
snapshot_reconciliation.runtime_coverage: R3 S03 verifies safe-forward from genesis prefix; S04 verifies ahead failure; S05 separately verifies equal-sequence head and spent divergence. Other prefix/classification paths have offline pure tests; malformed archive recovery is not an added Linux runtime case.

limitations: No resistance to rolling back BOTH ledger and snapshot to older mutually consistent history.
S01/S02/S04/S05 retain startup exit/probe observation JSON plus raw traceback and matching source; this is application evidence, not an OS trace.
S03 captures the restored S0 bytes before restart as well as preserved L1 and recovery output.
R3 preserves the harness/config manifests and their hash; OS-level execution attestation is not claimed.
